1	## Chapters
2	
3	### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains
4	
5	**Tutorial:**
6	
7	1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
8	2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
9	3. “Select Lyn.”
10	4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
11	5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
12	6. “Select attack!”
13	7. “Select Lyn.”
14	8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
15	9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
16	10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
17	11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.
18	
19	**Agent notes:**
20	
21	- Attempt 1 (s01) LOST: Lyn (16 HP, iron sword, 5 dmg x2) vs Batta (21 HP, 10 dmg, 40% hit) on his gate. Batta needs ~3 of Lyn's rounds; two 40% hits kill her. Batta never leaves the gate. Do NOT stand next to him below 16 HP and never take two rounds in a row: attack once, then next turn step away out of reach (he does not move) and use a vulnerary, then return. Lyn has 2 vulneraries x3.
22	- Attempt 2 (s01) WON, no losses: Lyn waited on the forest tile she starts on until the bandit came adjacent, then killed it. Vs Batta: end the turn standing NEXT to him with Wait (he gets one swing per enemy phase, Lyn's counter does 10). Heal if HP<=10. Two enemy phases brought him to 3 HP, then one attack finished him. Seize = move onto the gate tile he stood on.
23	- No tutorial prompts appeared (tutorial looks off). Tactician name is "Claude". Saved to slot 1 after the chapter.
24	- Cursor box draws slightly above/left of the tile it is on; check the terrain window. Lyn starts ~5 tiles from first bandit; letting him come, then attacking, cost her 10 HP.
25	
26	### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate
27	
28	**Tutorial:**
29	
30	1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
31	2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
32	3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
33	4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
34	5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
35	6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
36	7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
37	   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
38	8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
39	9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
40	10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
41	11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
42	12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!
43	
44	**Agent notes:**
45	
46	- Attempt 1 (s02) WON, no losses, 13 turns. Tutorial prompts did not appear. Kent (sword) and Lyn kill bandits easily; Sain (lance vs axe) is weak and dropped to 7 HP — keep him back. Kent and Sain each carry vulneraries too (check items).
47	- Boss Zugu (23 HP, 8 dmg, 48% hit) sits at the top-right past the north bridge and never moves. Kent at full HP with iron sword (8 dmg, 100% hit) beat him alone: attack, let him swing in enemy phase (counter), attack again.
48	- Input quirk: the cursor/arrow on screenshots can lag; if A doesn't confirm a move, nudge the cursor off and back. After an attack a highlighted box sometimes appears; B clears it. Using an item on a cavalier leaves Canto active; stray directional presses then move him.
49	- Saved to slot 1 after the chapter.

51	### Chapter 2 — Sword of Spirits
52	
53	**Tutorial:**
54	
55	1. The three buildings to the south are homes. You can speak with the people who live there. They sometimes give you combat hints or useful information about the land and the people. It pays to listen!
56	2. Next, send Sain to visit another home. Start by selecting Sain.
57	3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
58	4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
59	5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
60	6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
61	7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
62	8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
63	9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!
64	
65	**Agent notes:**
66	
67	- Attempt 1 (s03) WON, no losses, 13 turns. The two buildings top-left (near start) are NOT visitable (one is a Fort, good for Sain). Kent visited the house bottom-left (directly below him).
68	- Bandits trickle in from the north and south; parking Kent (sword) where they come and attacking on player phase handled all of them. Sain (lance) is weak vs axes.
69	- The castle is sealed: the cracked tile on its LEFT wall (row of the starting units, ~col 8) is a breakable wall. Kent broke it in 3 hits (from the tile west of it). The axe guard inside then walks out and dies.
70	- Boss Glass: 20 HP, Str 5, Def 3, iron sword, sits on the throne and never moves. Sain (iron lance) does 11 dmg, takes 3: two rounds killed him. Then Lyn walks in and Seizes.
71	- Throne approach: only from the tile directly below it; keep that tile clear for Lyn.
72	- No save prompt appeared after the chapter. Pressing A through the ending runs straight into Ch3's turn 1 and A starts selecting Lyn - stop batching A once the map shows.
73	
74	### Chapter 3 — Band of Mercenaries
75	
76	**Tutorial:**
77	
78	1. The red-roofed buildings are villages. Villages are in danger of being attacked.
79	2. If an enemy unit reaches a village before one of our units does, the village will be destroyed.
80	3. As quickly as possible, visit the residents and give them warning. Only good can come of it. So, let’s visit them.
81	4. Please select Lyn.
82	5. By visiting a village, we gained a new companion. Wil is an archer. He uses a bow to fight.
83	6. Bows can be fired at foes more than 1 space away. Obstacles won’t affect your line of fire.
84	7. Attacking enemies without moving next to them is called indirect combat.
85	8. If the enemy has no weapons capable of indirect combat, there’s no fear of counterattack, and that’s to our benefit.
86	9. However, you cannot fire on adjacent spaces. If someone moves next to you and attacks, that’s it.
87	10. Units with bows are best suited to lend assistance from the rear. Let’s try some indirect combat, shall we?
88	11. Select Wil.
89	12. Next is Florina, a pegasus knight. As you might guess, pegasus knights have the ability to fly. They can move over almost any terrain type. This small wall would stop most units, but it poses no problem for a pegasus knight. Select Florina.
90	13. Knowing your units and their abilities and knowing how to use them in battle is a shortcut to victory.
91	14. To learn everything about a unit, place the cursor on that unit and press the R Button.
92	15. Weapons have the strength to be used only a limited number of times. As you fight, their endurance drops.
93	16. At zero, the weapon breaks and disappears from your inventory.
94	17. Check your weapon endurance by placing the cursor on a unit and pressing the R Button.
95	18. You can also check on the item screen.
96	19. The number next to the weapon is its endurance. Be careful. Without a weapon a unit cannot enter combat.
97	20. Units that fly, like pegasus knights, are very vulnerable to bow attacks.
98	21. Arrows will deal critical damage to them.
99	22. If the enemy has bow-wielding units, you must be extremely cautious.
100	
101	**Agent notes:**
102	
103	- Attempt 1 (s04) WON, no losses, 11 turns. Lyn visits the village right above her start (door 2 right, 2 up) on turn 1 -> Wil joins. Tutorial prompts did not appear.
104	- The top-left village is NOT reachable from the start area (cliffs); a bandit razed it on ~turn 4. Accept the loss or don't bother.
105	- Held a tight group around the starting village and let enemies come; archers and swordsmen came first. Kent/Sain cleaned up, Wil chipped from 2 tiles. Florina kept back bottom-left all chapter (archers).
106	- Watch Sain/Kent HP: they dropped to 5-6 HP from enemy-phase hits. Lyn has NO vulneraries (only Iron sword + Mani Katti); Kent and Sain each carry 2.
107	- The way north is the grass gap at column 11 (east of the walls). The building at right-middle is an Armory, not a fort.
108	- Boss Migal (Brigand, 25 HP, Def 5, steel axe, 10 dmg / 37% hit vs Kent) sits at the top-right (col 13, row 0) and does not move. The tile under him is a ruin wall; reach him from the ruins tile below. Kent (iron sword, 8x2) took him to ~9 HP on player phase, then his enemy-phase counter killed him.
109	- Input quirk: A presses with frames=3 sometimes don't register on the move-target; plain A works. A pressed with the cursor on an empty tile opens the map menu (End is the 5th entry).
110	- No save prompt appeared after the chapter.
111	
112	### Chapter 4 — In Occupation's Shadow
113	
114	**Tutorial:**
115	
116	1. “In this chapter, your goal is to protect a special character for a set period of time. Keep Natalie safe for 7 turns. Natalie, and other green units are called NPCs. NPCs are not enemies, but they cannot be moved or given orders. Sometimes, green units will be attacked because they are on the field of combat. Be careful not to let enemies close in on Natalie.”
117	2. “When the enemy far outnumbers your group, it’s safer to restrict the battle to smaller areas. No matter how strong an enemy is, if he’s attacked on all sides, he’s sure to take massive damage. So, the east door is Lyn’s, and the south door is everyone else’s. Be on guard. Select Lyn, move her to the space indicated by the cursor, and have her wait.”
118	3. “Sometimes, you can speak with enemy characters. If you think you can converse with someone, move one of your units to an adjacent space. By and large, you’ll know whom to send from hints you receive in other conversations. When you’re not sure, just try using Lyn. Select Lyn now.”
119	4. “In this way, you can sometimes turn enemies into allies. Never underestimate the power of persuasive speech. Your new companion, Dorcas, is an axe-wielding fighter. Do you remember the weapon triangle? Axes are strong against lances and weak against swords. Axes have more power than other weapons, but they are also more difficult to hit with. Try using Dorcas to attack. Select Dorcas now.”
120	5. “The weapon Dorcas is wielding is called a handaxe. Use it to attack an adjacent opponent, or throw it in indirect combat in the manner of a bow. This versatility makes it a valuable weapon. It’s difficult to hit with, though, so don’t rely on it too much. Now let’s use the handaxe and try some indirect combat.”
121	6. “Right now, after all of your units have moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn, right? Sometimes, there are moments when you might not want or be able to move all your units. When it’s bothersome to tell your units to wait one by one, select end from the map menu to speed things up. To display the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button.”
122	
123	**Agent notes:**
124	
125	- Attempt 1 (s05) LOST on the very last enemy phase (turn 7): Natalie killed. Sain died turn 3 (lance at south door vs axes), Florina died turn 7 guarding Natalie.
126	- Layout: Natalie stands in a 1-wide alcove at the top-middle of the fort; the ONLY tile next to her is directly below her. Put a sturdy unit there (Lyn at full HP or Kent with sword), NEVER Florina - bandits (axes) kill her, then reach Natalie.
127	- The fort's WEST wall (left side, near Natalie's row) is cracked: bandits outside hit it from turn 2 and break through ~turn 6; two bandits then walk in from the west toward Natalie. Plan for that.
128	- South door = 2 tiles wide (bottom-middle). East door = upper-right. Enemies (Dorcas, a bandit, mercenaries) come in the east door from turn 2-3.
129	- Dorcas (fighter, recruitable) enters via east door ~turn 3 with a bandit beside him. Lyn: move next to him and Talk -> he joins (30 HP, hand axe, 1 vulnerary).
130	- Kent's iron sword had only 3 uses at chapter start; Lyn's iron sword (31) was traded to him. After trading, use Item > Equip so he isn't stuck with the lance.
131	- Wil from 2 tiles kills weakened bandits/mercs well. Lyn took 10 dmg standing near east door on turn 1 - keep her back first.
132	- Options: set Animation OFF (Map menu > Options) - saves lots of time.
133	- SAVE PROMPT WARNING: after Ch3 the game DOES show a Save screen, but pressing Start through the ending skips it. s04 skipped it, so the slot still held Ch3 and after the Ch4 game over Restart Chapter replayed all of Ch3 (s05 had to beat Ch3 again, then saved). After every chapter, press A (not Start) near the end and watch for the Save screen; choose slot 1 > Save.
134	- Attempt 2 (s05) WON. Key layout fact: Natalie sits at the top of a 1-wide corridor (Natalie, then 2 corridor tiles below her, then the big hall). Put Lyn on the tile directly under Natalie and a cavalier on the tile under Lyn on turn 1 and NEVER move them: nothing can reach Natalie. Natalie never took a hit.
135	- Danger in that setup: Dorcas (hand axe, range 1-2) stood in the hall below the corridor and hit Lyn over the cavalier's head (Lyn 18 -> 8). The cavalier in the corridor is boxed in once an enemy stands below him, so Lyn cannot get out to Talk to Dorcas. Give Lyn a vulnerary on turn 1 (trade from Kent/Sain) and check her HP every turn. Dorcas was NOT recruited (he leaves after the chapter).
136	- Units outside the corridor get swarmed: ~6 bandits pour through the 2-wide south door on turns 1-2, plus archers/mercs and the west-wall breach. Florina (turn 4, west inner corridor next to the cracked wall) and Wil (turn 7, trapped in the hall at 4 HP) both fell. They 'retreat' in Lyn's story (they reappear in cutscenes) but are recorded in dead. Next time keep Wil/Florina out of the hall - e.g. hold them inside the corridor area or have a cavalier Rescue one.
137	- Kent's iron sword broke during Ch4 (he only has an Iron lance now). Lyn has Iron sword + Mani Katti + a vulnerary.
138	- Ch4 ending: no Save screen was seen (A-presses may have passed it). Text speed resets; A presses in the Ch5 intro run straight onto the map and A selects Lyn - stop pressing once the map shows.
139	
140	
141	### Chapter 5 — Beyond the Borders
142	
143	**Tutorial:**
144	
145	1. “Sometimes, you can talk to different NPCs (the green units on the map). The process is the same as talking to enemies. Give it a try. Please select Lyn. (Lyn selected)”
146	2. Erk, a mage, and Serra, a cleric, have joined your group. Mages use the magic of truth to attack and damage their enemies. Clerics use staves to restore HP to their allies. Let’s try them both. First, select Serra.
147	3. Press the A button, and select the staff from the menu.
148	4. “Clerics cannot wield weapons; therefore they can’t engage in combat. However, they can use their staves to restore HP to allied units. Besides healing staves, which restore HP, there are other staves with different abilities. It’s always a good idea to test out any new abilities you receive, so let’s do that now. Have Erk demonstrate his magic. Begin by selecting Erk.”
149	5. “Magic, like Dorcas’s throwing axes, can strike enemies in adjacent squares as well as those at a distance. It’s very useful. Magic can penetrate even the strongest defenses, so it can be used in many situations. However, mages have few HP and low defensive abilities. To avoid counter-attacks, move in close to archers, and attack other fighters from 1 space away. Try and formulate combat strategies like this to be successful on the field of combat.”
150	
151	**Agent notes:**
152	
153	- Attempt 1 (s06) WON, no losses, 11 turns. Army was only Lyn, Sain, Erk, Serra (Kent absent). Objective: Defeat all enemies (7).
154	- Turn 1: Lyn walks 2 right next to Serra and Talks -> Erk + Serra join. Sain one-shot the archer next to the start.
155	- Enemies trickle in a few at a time; Lyn (doubles bandits with sword vs axe) + Erk handled them. Serra heal staff fixes chip damage.
156	- Boss Bug (Brigand, 29 HP, Def 8, Res 0, Steel axe) at bottom-right (~col 14, row 9) never moved. Erk from 2 tiles directly above him (col 14 row 7) did 10 dmg/turn at 90% with no counter: 3 turns, kill.
157	- Villages: one next to the first bandit (Erk visited, tutorial talk), top-right one Lyn visited, bottom-middle one (Sain) only tips; the building at right of row 3 is an Armory.
158	- No Save screen was seen after Ch5 either (pressed A in batches of 10-20). Ch6 intro ends straight on the map at turn 1 (objective: Hit switches).
159	- Input quirk: after a unit acts, extra A presses open the map menu/unit list; use B to back out. After End, the cursor starts on Lyn.
160	
161	### Chapter 6 — Blood of Pride
162	
163	**Tutorial:**
164	
165	1. The goal of this chapter is to open the doors and reach the 3 triggers located inside. To open doors, you need door keys or the services of a thief.
166	2. There may be times when you are unsure how to proceed. Start by checking Status on the Map Menu. Visiting homes or villages is also a good way to get information. Who knows what hints you might find. Let’s try visiting a house. Please select Lyn.
167	3. The thief Matthew has joined your group. Thieves have picks, which they use to open doors and chests. Picks are usable by thieves alone. It’s time to open that door. Select Matthew.
168	4. The door has been opened. With that, you can also see inside the room behind the door. Within the room there’s a different-colored floor tile. Tiles that seem different in some way might be the triggers we’re looking for. Select Rath, move him to that tile, and order him to wait. Triggers can be released by having allied units wait on them.
169	5. Thieves can use their picks to open chests. Move Matthew onto the chest, and the chest command will appear. Choose this command, and the contents of the chest will become yours. Why don’t we see what we can find? Go ahead and select Matthew.
170	6. An angelic robe increases a character’s max HP by a small amount. Select the item on the item list and use it. To view more detailed information on items, press the R Button on the item list. A thief has the skill to open doors and chests, right? That ability can only be utilized if the thief has a set of picks. The number next to an item is the number of times the item can be used before the item breaks. Keep that in mind.
171	7. If you get a weapon or staff you can’t use, don’t worry. Other members of your party might be able to wield them. Items you cannot use appear in gray text. Try trading these items to others in your group. Don’t forget: you can only trade items with one other character at a time.
172	
173	**Agent notes:**
174	
175	- Attempt 1 (s07) WON, no losses, 14 turns. Army: Lyn, Sain, Rath (nomad, bow), Erk, Serra; Matthew joins turn 3 (cutscene after Lyn visits the house next to the start - that house also gives Lyn a Door key). There is NO Kent this chapter (the cavalier with a lance is Sain).
176	- Enemies are few (≈8) and mostly passive. Switch 1: room behind the door just NE of the start (Matthew picks it, Rath walks on). Switch 2: SE room, door opened with Lyn's key; a lance bandit stands on it. Switch 3: under boss Bool (26 HP, Steel lance, 16 dmg) in the top-middle room, which opens after switch 2 along with an archer. Bool never moves.

## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s01) LOST: Lyn (16 HP, iron sword, 5 dmg x2) vs Batta (21 HP, 10 dmg, 40% hit) on his gate. Batta needs ~3 of Lyn's rounds; two 40% hits kill her. Batta never leaves the gate. Do NOT stand next to him below 16 HP and never take two rounds in a row: attack once, then next turn step away out of reach (he does not move) and use a vulnerary, then return. Lyn has 2 vulneraries x3.
- Attempt 2 (s01) WON, no losses: Lyn waited on the forest tile she starts on until the bandit came adjacent, then killed it. Vs Batta: end the turn standing NEXT to him with Wait (he gets one swing per enemy phase, Lyn's counter does 10). Heal if HP<=10. Two enemy phases brought him to 3 HP, then one attack finished him. Seize = move onto the gate tile he stood on.
- No tutorial prompts appeared (tutorial looks off). Tactician name is "Claude". Saved to slot 1 after the chapter.
- Cursor box draws slightly above/left of the tile it is on; check the terrain window. Lyn starts ~5 tiles from first bandit; letting him come, then attacking, cost her 10 HP.

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s02) WON, no losses, 13 turns. Tutorial prompts did not appear. Kent (sword) and Lyn kill bandits easily; Sain (lance vs axe) is weak and dropped to 7 HP — keep him back. Kent and Sain each carry vulneraries too (check items).
- Boss Zugu (23 HP, 8 dmg, 48% hit) sits at the top-right past the north bridge and never moves. Kent at full HP with iron sword (8 dmg, 100% hit) beat him alone: attack, let him swing in enemy phase (counter), attack again.
- Input quirk: the cursor/arrow on screenshots can lag; if A doesn't confirm a move, nudge the cursor off and back. After an attack a highlighted box sometimes appears; B clears it. Using an item on a cavalier leaves Canto active; stray directional presses then move him.
- Saved to slot 1 after the chapter.

### Chapter 2 — Sword of Spirits

**Tutorial:**

1. The three buildings to the south are homes. You can speak with the people who live there. They sometimes give you combat hints or useful information about the land and the people. It pays to listen!
2. Next, send Sain to visit another home. Start by selecting Sain.
3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s03) WON, no losses, 13 turns. The two buildings top-left (near start) are NOT visitable (one is a Fort, good for Sain). Kent visited the house bottom-left (directly below him).
- Bandits trickle in from the north and south; parking Kent (sword) where they come and attacking on player phase handled all of them. Sain (lance) is weak vs axes.
- The castle is sealed: the cracked tile on its LEFT wall (row of the starting units, ~col 8) is a breakable wall. Kent broke it in 3 hits (from the tile west of it). The axe guard inside then walks out and dies.
- Boss Glass: 20 HP, Str 5, Def 3, iron sword, sits on the throne and never moves. Sain (iron lance) does 11 dmg, takes 3: two rounds killed him. Then Lyn walks in and Seizes.
- Throne approach: only from the tile directly below it; keep that tile clear for Lyn.
- No save prompt appeared after the chapter. Pressing A through the ending runs straight into Ch3's turn 1 and A starts selecting Lyn - stop batching A once the map shows.

### Chapter 3 — Band of Mercenaries

**Tutorial:**

1. The red-roofed buildings are villages. Villages are in danger of being attacked.
2. If an enemy unit reaches a village before one of our units does, the village will be destroyed.
3. As quickly as possible, visit the residents and give them warning. Only good can come of it. So, let’s visit them.
4. Please select Lyn.
5. By visiting a village, we gained a new companion. Wil is an archer. He uses a bow to fight.
6. Bows can be fired at foes more than 1 space away. Obstacles won’t affect your line of fire.
7. Attacking enemies without moving next to them is called indirect combat.
8. If the enemy has no weapons capable of indirect combat, there’s no fear of counterattack, and that’s to our benefit.
9. However, you cannot fire on adjacent spaces. If someone moves next to you and attacks, that’s it.
10. Units with bows are best suited to lend assistance from the rear. Let’s try some indirect combat, shall we?
11. Select Wil.
12. Next is Florina, a pegasus knight. As you might guess, pegasus knights have the ability to fly. They can move over almost any terrain type. This small wall would stop most units, but it poses no problem for a pegasus knight. Select Florina.
13. Knowing your units and their abilities and knowing how to use them in battle is a shortcut to victory.
14. To learn everything about a unit, place the cursor on that unit and press the R Button.
15. Weapons have the strength to be used only a limited number of times. As you fight, their endurance drops.
16. At zero, the weapon breaks and disappears from your inventory.
17. Check your weapon endurance by placing the cursor on a unit and pressing the R Button.
18. You can also check on the item screen.
19. The number next to the weapon is its endurance. Be careful. Without a weapon a unit cannot enter combat.
20. Units that fly, like pegasus knights, are very vulnerable to bow attacks.
21. Arrows will deal critical damage to them.
22. If the enemy has bow-wielding units, you must be extremely cautious.

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s04) WON, no losses, 11 turns. Lyn visits the village right above her start (door 2 right, 2 up) on turn 1 -> Wil joins. Tutorial prompts did not appear.
- The top-left village is NOT reachable from the start area (cliffs); a bandit razed it on ~turn 4. Accept the loss or don't bother.
- Held a tight group around the starting village and let enemies come; archers and swordsmen came first. Kent/Sain cleaned up, Wil chipped from 2 tiles. Florina kept back bottom-left all chapter (archers).

## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s01) LOST: Lyn (16 HP, iron sword, 5 dmg x2) vs Batta (21 HP, 10 dmg, 40% hit) on his gate. Batta needs ~3 of Lyn's rounds; two 40% hits kill her. Batta never leaves the gate. Do NOT stand next to him below 16 HP and never take two rounds in a row: attack once, then next turn step away out of reach (he does not move) and use a vulnerary, then return. Lyn has 2 vulneraries x3.
- Attempt 2 (s01) WON, no losses: Lyn waited on the forest tile she starts on until the bandit came adjacent, then killed it. Vs Batta: end the turn standing NEXT to him with Wait (he gets one swing per enemy phase, Lyn's counter does 10). Heal if HP<=10. Two enemy phases brought him to 3 HP, then one attack finished him. Seize = move onto the gate tile he stood on.
- No tutorial prompts appeared (tutorial looks off). Tactician name is "Claude". Saved to slot 1 after the chapter.
- Cursor box draws slightly above/left of the tile it is on; check the terrain window. Lyn starts ~5 tiles from first bandit; letting him come, then attacking, cost her 10 HP.

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.

## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s01) LOST: Lyn (16 HP, iron sword, 5 dmg x2) vs Batta (21 HP, 10 dmg, 40% hit) on his gate. Batta needs ~3 of Lyn's rounds; two 40% hits kill her. Batta never leaves the gate. Do NOT stand next to him below 16 HP and never take two rounds in a row: attack once, then next turn step away out of reach (he does not move) and use a vulnerary, then return. Lyn has 2 vulneraries x3.
- Attempt 2 (s01) WON, no losses: Lyn waited on the forest tile she starts on until the bandit came adjacent, then killed it. Vs Batta: end the turn standing NEXT to him with Wait (he gets one swing per enemy phase, Lyn's counter does 10). Heal if HP<=10. Two enemy phases brought him to 3 HP, then one attack finished him. Seize = move onto the gate tile he stood on.
- No tutorial prompts appeared (tutorial looks off). Tactician name is "Claude". Saved to slot 1 after the chapter.
- Cursor box draws slightly above/left of the tile it is on; check the terrain window. Lyn starts ~5 tiles from first bandit; letting him come, then attacking, cost her 10 HP.

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s02) WON, no losses, 13 turns. Tutorial prompts did not appear. Kent (sword) and Lyn kill bandits easily; Sain (lance vs axe) is weak and dropped to 7 HP — keep him back. Kent and Sain each carry vulneraries too (check items).
- Boss Zugu (23 HP, 8 dmg, 48% hit) sits at the top-right past the north bridge and never moves. Kent at full HP with iron sword (8 dmg, 100% hit) beat him alone: attack, let him swing in enemy phase (counter), attack again.
- Input quirk: the cursor/arrow on screenshots can lag; if A doesn't confirm a move, nudge the cursor off and back. After an attack a highlighted box sometimes appears; B clears it. Using an item on a cavalier leaves Canto active; stray directional presses then move him.
- Saved to slot 1 after the chapter.

### Chapter 2 — Sword of Spirits

**Tutorial:**

1. The three buildings to the south are homes. You can speak with the people who live there. They sometimes give you combat hints or useful information about the land and the people. It pays to listen!
2. Next, send Sain to visit another home. Start by selecting Sain.
3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s03) WON, no losses, 13 turns. The two buildings top-left (near start) are NOT visitable (one is a Fort, good for Sain). Kent visited the house bottom-left (directly below him).
- Bandits trickle in from the north and south; parking Kent (sword) where they come and attacking on player phase handled all of them. Sain (lance) is weak vs axes.
- The castle is sealed: the cracked tile on its LEFT wall (row of the starting units, ~col 8) is a breakable wall. Kent broke it in 3 hits (from the tile west of it). The axe guard inside then walks out and dies.
- Boss Glass: 20 HP, Str 5, Def 3, iron sword, sits on the throne and never moves. Sain (iron lance) does 11 dmg, takes 3: two rounds killed him. Then Lyn walks in and Seizes.
- Throne approach: only from the tile directly below it; keep that tile clear for Lyn.
- No save prompt appeared after the chapter. Pressing A through the ending runs straight into Ch3's turn 1 and A starts selecting Lyn - stop batching A once the map shows.

### Chapter 3 — Band of Mercenaries

**Tutorial:**

1. The red-roofed buildings are villages. Villages are in danger of being attacked.
2. If an enemy unit reaches a village before one of our units does, the village will be destroyed.
3. As quickly as possible, visit the residents and give them warning. Only good can come of it. So, let’s visit them.
4. Please select Lyn.
5. By visiting a village, we gained a new companion. Wil is an archer. He uses a bow to fight.
6. Bows can be fired at foes more than 1 space away. Obstacles won’t affect your line of fire.
7. Attacking enemies without moving next to them is called indirect combat.
8. If the enemy has no weapons capable of indirect combat, there’s no fear of counterattack, and that’s to our benefit.
9. However, you cannot fire on adjacent spaces. If someone moves next to you and attacks, that’s it.
10. Units with bows are best suited to lend assistance from the rear. Let’s try some indirect combat, shall we?
11. Select Wil.
12. Next is Florina, a pegasus knight. As you might guess, pegasus knights have the ability to fly. They can move over almost any terrain type. This small wall would stop most units, but it poses no problem for a pegasus knight. Select Florina.
13. Knowing your units and their abilities and knowing how to use them in battle is a shortcut to victory.
14. To learn everything about a unit, place the cursor on that unit and press the R Button.
15. Weapons have the strength to be used only a limited number of times. As you fight, their endurance drops.
16. At zero, the weapon breaks and disappears from your inventory.
17. Check your weapon endurance by placing the cursor on a unit and pressing the R Button.
18. You can also check on the item screen.
19. The number next to the weapon is its endurance. Be careful. Without a weapon a unit cannot enter combat.
20. Units that fly, like pegasus knights, are very vulnerable to bow attacks.
21. Arrows will deal critical damage to them.
22. If the enemy has bow-wielding units, you must be extremely cautious.

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s04) WON, no losses, 11 turns. Lyn visits the village right above her start (door 2 right, 2 up) on turn 1 -> Wil joins. Tutorial prompts did not appear.
- The top-left village is NOT reachable from the start area (cliffs); a bandit razed it on ~turn 4. Accept the loss or don't bother.
- Held a tight group around the starting village and let enemies come; archers and swordsmen came first. Kent/Sain cleaned up, Wil chipped from 2 tiles. Florina kept back bottom-left all chapter (archers).
- Watch Sain/Kent HP: they dropped to 5-6 HP from enemy-phase hits. Lyn has NO vulneraries (only Iron sword + Mani Katti); Kent and Sain each carry 2.
- The way north is the grass gap at column 11 (east of the walls). The building at right-middle is an Armory, not a fort.
- Boss Migal (Brigand, 25 HP, Def 5, steel axe, 10 dmg / 37% hit vs Kent) sits at the top-right (col 13, row 0) and does not move. The tile under him is a ruin wall; reach him from the ruins tile below. Kent (iron sword, 8x2) took him to ~9 HP on player phase, then his enemy-phase counter killed him.
- Input quirk: A presses with frames=3 sometimes don't register on the move-target; plain A works. A pressed with the cursor on an empty tile opens the map menu (End is the 5th entry).
- No save prompt appeared after the chapter.

### Chapter 4 — In Occupation's Shadow

**Tutorial:**

1. “In this chapter, your goal is to protect a special character for a set period of time. Keep Natalie safe for 7 turns. Natalie, and other green units are called NPCs. NPCs are not enemies, but they cannot be moved or given orders. Sometimes, green units will be attacked because they are on the field of combat. Be careful not to let enemies close in on Natalie.”
2. “When the enemy far outnumbers your group, it’s safer to restrict the battle to smaller areas. No matter how strong an enemy is, if he’s attacked on all sides, he’s sure to take massive damage. So, the east door is Lyn’s, and the south door is everyone else’s. Be on guard. Select Lyn, move her to the space indicated by the cursor, and have her wait.”
3. “Sometimes, you can speak with enemy characters. If you think you can converse with someone, move one of your units to an adjacent space. By and large, you’ll know whom to send from hints you receive in other conversations. When you’re not sure, just try using Lyn. Select Lyn now.”
4. “In this way, you can sometimes turn enemies into allies. Never underestimate the power of persuasive speech. Your new companion, Dorcas, is an axe-wielding fighter. Do you remember the weapon triangle? Axes are strong against lances and weak against swords. Axes have more power than other weapons, but they are also more difficult to hit with. Try using Dorcas to attack. Select Dorcas now.”
5. “The weapon Dorcas is wielding is called a handaxe. Use it to attack an adjacent opponent, or throw it in indirect combat in the manner of a bow. This versatility makes it a valuable weapon. It’s difficult to hit with, though, so don’t rely on it too much. Now let’s use the handaxe and try some indirect combat.”
6. “Right now, after all of your units have moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn, right? Sometimes, there are moments when you might not want or be able to move all your units. When it’s bothersome to tell your units to wait one by one, select end from the map menu to speed things up. To display the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button.”

**Agent notes:**

- Attempt 1 (s05) LOST on the very last enemy phase (turn 7): Natalie killed. Sain died turn 3 (lance at south door vs axes), Florina died turn 7 guarding Natalie.
- Layout: Natalie stands in a 1-wide alcove at the top-middle of the fort; the ONLY tile next to her is directly below her. Put a sturdy unit there (Lyn at full HP or Kent with sword), NEVER Florina - bandits (axes) kill her, then reach Natalie.
- The fort's WEST wall (left side, near Natalie's row) is cracked: bandits outside hit it from turn 2 and break through ~turn 6; two bandits then walk in from the west toward Natalie. Plan for that.
- South door = 2 tiles wide (bottom-middle). East door = upper-right. Enemies (Dorcas, a bandit, mercenaries) come in the east door from turn 2-3.
- Dorcas (fighter, recruitable) enters via east door ~turn 3 with a bandit beside him. Lyn: move next to him and Talk -> he joins (30 HP, hand axe, 1 vulnerary).
- Kent's iron sword had only 3 uses at chapter start; Lyn's iron sword (31) was traded to him. After trading, use Item > Equip so he isn't stuck with the lance.
- Wil from 2 tiles kills weakened bandits/mercs well. Lyn took 10 dmg standing near east door on turn 1 - keep her back first.
- Options: set Animation OFF (Map menu > Options) - saves lots of time.
- SAVE PROMPT WARNING: after Ch3 the game DOES show a Save screen, but pressing Start through the ending skips it. s04 skipped it, so the slot still held Ch3 and after the Ch4 game over Restart Chapter replayed all of Ch3 (s05 had to beat Ch3 again, then saved). After every chapter, press A (not Start) near the end and watch for the Save screen; choose slot 1 > Save.
- Attempt 2 (s05) WON. Key layout fact: Natalie sits at the top of a 1-wide corridor (Natalie, then 2 corridor tiles below her, then the big hall). Put Lyn on the tile directly under Natalie and a cavalier on the tile under Lyn on turn 1 and NEVER move them: nothing can reach Natalie. Natalie never took a hit.
- Danger in that setup: Dorcas (hand axe, range 1-2) stood in the hall below the corridor and hit Lyn over the cavalier's head (Lyn 18 -> 8). The cavalier in the corridor is boxed in once an enemy stands below him, so Lyn cannot get out to Talk to Dorcas. Give Lyn a vulnerary on turn 1 (trade from Kent/Sain) and check her HP every turn. Dorcas was NOT recruited (he leaves after the chapter).
- Units outside the corridor get swarmed: ~6 bandits pour through the 2-wide south door on turns 1-2, plus archers/mercs and the west-wall breach. Florina (turn 4, west inner corridor next to the cracked wall) and Wil (turn 7, trapped in the hall at 4 HP) both fell. They 'retreat' in Lyn's story (they reappear in cutscenes) but are recorded in dead. Next time keep Wil/Florina out of the hall - e.g. hold them inside the corridor area or have a cavalier Rescue one.
- Kent's iron sword broke during Ch4 (he only has an Iron lance now). Lyn has Iron sword + Mani Katti + a vulnerary.
- Ch4 ending: no Save screen was seen (A-presses may have passed it). Text speed resets; A presses in the Ch5 intro run straight onto the map and A selects Lyn - stop pressing once the map shows.


### Chapter 5 — Beyond the Borders

**Agent notes:**

- TOP NOOK = 2 deck tiles ABOVE the Merlinus tile and the window tile. Each is reachable only from below + by flyers from the side.

Merlinus retreated EP3; a shaman then stood on his tile and Flux'd Lyn (23->15). T4 Lyn stepped down to kill it (killed, but she took 8 -> 7 HP) and died EP4 to the myrmidon below her. **Agent notes:**

- (s29) Prep: only 5 slots (Hector, Eliwood, Oswin, Lyn, Sain). FOG OF WAR. DART (pirate, joins at start, Steel axe + Hand axe) - I gave his Hand axe to Hector T1 and Dart then had no ranged; Dart (16 HP) was left alone and DIED EP4. Keep Dart next to Oswin and retreat him when hurt.

UHAI (Nomadic Trooper, 33 HP, Killing Edge 24 atk/36 crit, Longbow, Short bow, Orion's bolt) sits in the forest at the BOTTOM-RIGHT, ~2 tiles from the east edge on the bottom row. He does NOT attack Oswin (0 dmg) but he DOES leave his tile later (~T31) and snipes others from the fog (took Sain 28->3 in one EP).
- Oswin (Hand axe) vs Uhai: 15 dmg, only 31% (16% when Uhai holds Killing Edge). Took ~8 turns per hit. Lyn's Mani Katti is effective but Killing Edge counter kills her. Hector Hammer: 12 dmg/36%; Uhai doubles a carrying Hector w/ Killing Edge (8x2, 23 crit) - dangerous.
- (s29 att.1 status at T45) Uhai at 18/33 HP and HIDING in fog since T32 (fog vision is only ~3 tiles). Searched with Oswin (immune): SE forest, centre, W of forest, N bridge, NE bridge area - not found yet. Sain 3/28 HP, Lyn 12/25 carried by Oswin, Eliwood carried by Hector at the S forest (bottom centre). No healing items at all. NEXT TIME: do NOT leave Uhai alone once found - once he's below half, keep Oswin adjacent and attack every turn; never let low-HP units within ~11 tiles of him.
- (s29 T51) FOUND: Uhai RETREATS TO A FORT when below ~half HP - the FORT is on the small river ISLAND with 2 ruined houses, WEST-CENTRE of the map (the island you pass on the way south, left of the first pink bridge). He healed to full there. So chip damage is useless: he must die in ONE player phase, or be hit hard enough to kill before he reaches the fort. KEY TRICK: Uhai's equipped weapon = the last one he used. When he holds a BOW (after shooting someone at range), melee attackers get NO counter - then dogpile with Lyn (Mani Katti effective), Hector, Sain, Eliwood (Rapier effective). When he holds the Killing Edge, only ranged attacks are safe.
- (s29 T60) WINNING IDEA: Uhai's only weapon left is the KILLING EDGE (14/20 at T60; his bows were gone). Oswin (General) takes 1 dmg (3 on crit) from it. Park Oswin ADJACENT to Uhai's fort and attack every turn with the Hand axe (melee) - each exchange + each enemy-phase attack burns 1-2 Killing Edge uses. When it BREAKS Uhai is weaponless -> everyone attacks freely. Fort is 2 tiles below 2 house tiles; Oswin stands on the house tile directly above the fort; Hector can stand on the tile above that (range 2, safe).

CONCLUSION: do NOT turtle. Next attempt try a RUSH: from T1 push Oswin+Hector up the N corridor -> through the door (Door key from the T2 archer drop) -> east grass band -> 1-tile gap below the throne (reached ~T19 in att.1 while turtling; should be ~T8 if rushing). Keep Lyn and Eliwood carried (Oswin carries Eliwood, Sain or Hector carries Lyn), and keep Sain glued to the group.
- (s30) ATT.2 LOST EP22: Hector (carrying Lyn, so halved Skl/Spd) got boxed in by the cavalier pack + myrmidon + paladin just N of the start corridor while trying to rush; died 31->5 over 3 EPs. - (s33 att.4) LYN CARRIES ORION'S BOLT (promotion item) - nobody used it before! Promote Lyn on T1 (Item > Orion's bolt): Blade Lord can use BOWS (Silver bow drops from the W-room archer T3; Oswin has a Longbow).
